question.leadin: Answer these questions about Japanese history.
question.text: The defeated Ishida said that he fought for the heir of this man. Known by the nicknames of "the monkey" and "the bald rat" because of his looks, his actions included the reunification of Japan and the invasion of Japan.
question.clue: He codified laws that crystallized the hierarchy of samurai, peasant, artisan, and merchant as well as ordering the 1588 Great Sword Hunt, ostensibly to decorate a temple enshrining himself.

swap.text: This Japanese admiral commanded the pilots at Pearl Harbor. His plane was shot down on Bougainville Island during Operation Vengeance in 1943.
swap.answerHtml: Isoroku Yamamoto [or Yamamoto Isoroku, since Japanese names are traditionally written in reverse order]
swap.clue: During the reign of Hirohito, this naval leader was opposed to signing the Tripartite Pact. However, he still orchestrated the surprise attack on Pearl Harbor.

question.leadin: Holders of this title, which originated in the Heian (hay-ahn) period, ruled from the Bakufu.
question.text: Holding power until the 1867 Meiji (may-jee) Restoration, name this title that denoted military rulers of Japan such as Ashikaga Takauji.
question.clue: After the arrival of the "black ships," the isolationist rule of this office was ended with the Convention of Kanagawa, shortly before they were made obsolete with the Meiji Restoration.

swap.text: The battle for this island, home to three Japanese air fields, saw the raising of an American flag on top of its Mount Suribachi.
swap.clue: During this battle, Tadamichi Kuribayashi prohibited banzai charges and instead created a system of tunnels inspired by his tactics at the Battle of Peleliu.

question.text: This American ended the policy of seclusion during the Tokugawa Shogunate after sailing into Tokyo harbor with his "Black Ships" and having the Convention of Kanagawa forcibly signed.
question.clue: This American naval officer who sailed into Tokyo Bay in 1853 in order to open Japan to large-scale international trade.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about things related to the history of Tokyo.
swap.text: This leader of the Japanese military during the second World War was hung in 1948. He previously led Japanese forces in Inner Mongolia and became chief of the Army General Staff during the war.
swap.clue: This leader of the Chahar Expeditionary Force ordered troops to attack Hebei Province following the Marco Polo incident.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Japanese history prior to the Meiji Restoration.
question.text: This city was the capital of Japan until Emperor Meiji made Tokyo the capital in 1868.
question.clue: Henry Stimson, the US Secretary of War, is said to have honeymooned here, and famously lobbied to have this city taken off the list of bombing targets during the Second World War despite significant protests from the military.

swap.leadin: Name some catalysts for reform in Japanese history, FTPE.
swap.text: This Japanese emperor oversaw the creation of the Diet and the modernization of Japan after the end of the Tokugawa Shogunate.
swap.clue: The short-lived Ezo Republic and Satsuma Rebellion were both attempts to counter progressive efforts undertaken during this period, which began after the Boshin War.

question.leadin: How many capitals of Japan are there? Only one. Nevertheless, there have been many ancient capitals of Japan.
question.text: This city names a period following the Asuka and was the first Japanese capital built in the Tang Chinese style. It was also the first permanent capital of Japan, before Nagaoka.
question.clue: This was the first time when emperors adopted the title of "tenno," and other innovations during this period, such as the institution of a Council of State, were adopted in order to imitate the government at Changan and important Tang Chinese institutions.

swap.text: This first Shogunate began after Minamoto Yoritomo defeated the Tairas at the Battle of Dannoura in 1185. It was late dominated by the Hojo family.
swap.clue: Its puppet rulers attempted to revolt with the Jokyu war, but were crushed and remained silent for another century.

question.text: The first major testing of the Meiji emperor was this rebellion of former samurai. It was led by Saigo Takamori, and it was named after a clan from Kyushu.
question.clue: Many leaders of this movement were on the losing side of the Seikanron Debate, in which they had unsuccessfully advocated a war, and thereafter they had resigned and returned to their home prefecture.

swap.text: Admirals Togo and Rozhestvensky faced off in this pivotal naval victory for Japan in the Russo-Japanese War, which was fought in the narrows between the Korean peninsula and Honshu.
swap.answerHtml: Battle of Tsushima Strait/s [or Tsusimskoye srazheniye; prompt on Battle of the Sea of Japan]
swap.clue: At the end of this battle, Admiral Nebogatov surrendered rather than doom his 2,000-plus sailors; regardless, his fleet had lost six battleships and twenty-eight other ships in a single day after eight months of sailing from the Baltic Sea.

question.text: This research group under the Kwantung Army committed some of the greatest Japanese crimes against humanity during the war. It was commanded by Shiro Ishii, who was pardoned by the United States after the war in exchange for his data.
question.answerHtml: Unit 731 [accept Nana-san-ichi Butai; accept Epidemic Prevention and Water Purification Department of the Kwantung Army; accept Kantogun Boeki Kyusuibu Honbu]
question.clue: This group within the Epidemic Prevention and Purification Department. A guy actually named Colonel Sanders brought it to the attention of Douglas MacArthur, who pardoned its leader in exchange for scientific data.

swap.leadin: During one of these events, soldiers fought on and around large walls at Iki-no-matsubara, and before these events a letter was sent addressed to the "ruler of a small country."
swap.text: Name these events chronicled by Suenaga, the second of which was repelled by a fleet-crushing "divine wind."
swap.answerHtml: Mongol invasions of Japan [or Yuan invasions of Japan; or Kublai Khan’s invasions of Japan; accept equivalents for invasion like “attack”; prompt on “Chinese invasion of Japan”; prompt on “invasions of Japan”]
swap.clue: During one of these conflicts, an exaggerated 142,000-strong army was defeated at the battle of Hakata Bay.

question.text: Landscapes and portraiture became more common in scroll art, and the predominant school of ikebana arose, during this period of Japanese history from 1337 to 1573.
question.clue: This shogunate that followed the Kenmu Restoration.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Rokuhara tandai.
swap.text: The Rokuhara tandai were a group of civil deputies who replaced the sbugo during this shogunate, which dates from the rise of Minamoto Yoritomo and was supplanted by the Ashikaga shogunate.
swap.clue: The capital was moved from this city to Kyoto during the Kenmu Restoration.

question.text: Rusk told Yang that the maritime Macarthur Line would hold until this 1951 treaty took effect. This treaty names the US's "system" of "hub and spokes" bilateral defense treaties with Pacific countries, especially Japan.
question.answerHtml: Treaty of San Francisco [or San Furanshisuko kōwa-Jōyaku; prompt on Treaty of Peace with Japan or U.S.-Japan Security Treaty (or Japanese equivalents) with “In what city was that treaty signed?]

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about the rise of a Japanese family.
swap.text: This family, most notably led by Yoritomo, rebelled against the Taira clan in 1180. Their victory led to the establishment of the first bakufu, or shogunate, and the start of the Kamakura period.
swap.clue: They were defeated by their main rivals in the Heiji Rebellion, after which many of them were mercifully sent into exile including Noriyori, the younger brother of the main members.

question.leadin: Answer the following about ancient legal codes.
question.text: This 645 CE set of policies promulgated in Japan shortly after the death of Prince Shotoku established the Ritsuryo, a strange mix of Legalistic laws and Confucian rhetoric adapted for Japanese conditions.
question.clue: The rapid expansion of the Tang and their allies in Korea caused panic in the Japanese imperial court, leading to a palace coup and subsequent political reforms spurred by this set of doctrines issued by Emperor Kotoku in 645.

swap.leadin: One of these structures is named after the Japanese word for chopsticks, Hashihaka, due to its resemblance to those utensils, and is thought to contain the body of the mythical queen Pimiko.
swap.text: Name these keyhole-shaped megalithic tombs in Japan. The era lasting from roughly the 3rd century to the 6th century is named for them.
swap.clue: A scholarly debate centers on whether two objects with raised left arms found in one of these places depict horse herders or dancers.
